title: Verified dual-sourcing optimal orders, region classification and reliability comparisons
contribution_type: Six complete Lean formalizations of established and explicitly repaired dual-sourcing statements

owner.source_commit_scope: Completed owning-project publication record and lifecycle; repository remains private. The exact accepted-proof source pin is separately preserved inside the archived packet.

claim: For the exact two-supplier random-capacity platform model: lattice submodularity, global maximizing-order existence with necessary stationarity, the exact CDF derivative, optimized-value reliability monotonicity, complete corrected deterministic-demand optimizer regions, and hedge-size/region reliability comparisons for the defined region functions. The latter two targets retain their distinct explicit hypotheses.

assumptions.suppliers: Two suppliers, indexed by Fin 2; positive finite design capacities.
assumptions.cost_parameters: 0 <= eta_i <= 1; r, p, c_i >= 0; v < r+p. These include disclosed platform additions.
assumptions.capacity_laws: For each reliability index, nonnegative atomless probability laws; CDF monotonicity in reliability is retained in Model.
assumptions.joint_law: The two capacity losses and demand are independent, through the exact product measure.
assumptions.feasible_orders: All componentwise nonnegative real vectors; no upper order cap is assumed.
assumptions.source_correspondence: The packet proves the complete platform signatures. The finite-mean and parameter qualifications supplied by the platform are disclosed; no equivalence to a broader unstated source theorem is claimed.
assumptions.demand_theorem_1_and_equation_6: Absolute continuity with respect to Lebesgue measure. Lemmas 1 and 2(b) require no demand density.
assumptions.equation_6_only: Feasible orders, distinct supplier indices i,j and a strictly interior coordinate 0<q_i<K_i.
assumptions.reliability_lemma_2b: The full Model CDF-order assumption is retained. No derivative or smoothness of the reliability-indexed laws is added; the conclusion concerns the optimized value, not every fixed order.
assumptions.random_demand_targets: Lemma1, Theorem1, Equation6 and Lemma2(b): a real probability law, nonnegative almost surely, with integrable identity. Theorem1/Equation6 additionally require absolute continuity.
assumptions.deterministic_theorem_2: Demand is dirac(x), x>=0; eta_i=0 and 0<phi_i<1. For each current reliability index there is 0<b_i<=K_i with G_i(b_i)=1 and a strictly increasing CDF on [0,b_i]. The explicit weighted full-capacity CDF supplier ordering is retained.
assumptions.corollary_1: eta_i=0, 0<phi_i<1, G_i(K_i,a)=1 at every reliability index and phi_2<=phi_1; vary one index upwards. Claims concern the exact hedgeRegion, singleRegion and qstarTotal definitions.
assumptions.corollary_interpretation: Corollary1 alone does not prove optimality of qstarTotal under laws lacking Theorem2 support assumptions. No strict contraction or coordinatewise ordering of individual optimal quantities is asserted.

limitations: Formalization of established and previously repaired statements; no mathematical novelty, exhaustive priority search, source-author endorsement or independent human review claimed.
Theorem2 proves the platform’s corrected min/max region bounds and explicit support/parameter assumptions. It does not establish the uncorrected printed statement.
Corollary1 concerns defined region and total-order functions under its own hypotheses; it does not assume Theorem2’s strict-support conditions. Optimality outside Theorem2 hypotheses is not claimed.
The corollary’s supplier2 single-source contraction is non-strict and follows by equality under G_i(K_i,a)=1. Individual optimal-quantity monotonicity (Lemma2(a)) remains outside this packet.
Necessary stationarity is not shown sufficient in the full random-demand setting; deterministic global optimality is proved separately.
The earlier appendix inspection used extracted text without an immutable binary snapshot. No proof equivalence to that appendix is claimed.
Verified pinned third-party caches are trusted inputs; this is not a Lean/Mathlib bootstrap verification.
